title: Claim a seat once, whatever the timing

blocks.text: The page's key point 7: a thread-safe collection does **not** make a check-then-act sequence atomic. `if (!map.containsKey(k)) map.put(k, v)` is two calls, and another thread can put `k` between them. The page's fix is a single atomic method on `ConcurrentHashMap`.

Write `Seats.claim(ConcurrentHashMap<String, String> seats, String seat, String person)`. If `seat` is free, `person` takes it. If it is taken, nothing changes. Either way it returns whoever holds the seat after the call. Two threads claiming the same free seat at the same moment must agree on one winner, and that winner must be the one in the map.

cases.says: Claiming a free seat gives it to the claimant, and claim returns the claimant.
A later claim on a taken seat changes nothing and returns the person who already holds it.
When two threads claim one free seat at the same moment, both calls return the same winner and the map holds that winner, even when both check the seat before either writes.

concepts: A thread-safe collection does not make a check-then-act sequence atomic; putIfAbsent does the check and the put as one step.
